_readme: THE MONITOR REGISTER — [pipeline E-9] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/11-measurement.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
Every hostname this factory serves, and whether anything is watching it.
WHY IT EXISTS. E-9's acceptance is 'every live hostname has a monitor, and the list cannot silently
shrink'. Until this file landed the right-hand side did not exist: the monitor set lived only inside
GlitchTip on the Oracle box, and the comparison the acceptance names was performed by a human, from
memory, when someone happened to look. Measured 2026-08-01 and again 2026-08-02: six monitors, five
hostnames, and TWO deployed custom domains — platform.nikatru.com and config.nikatru.com — that
nothing watches, both of them bound in services/platform/wrangler.jsonc since the day the Worker
shipped. Nobody had decided not to monitor them. Nobody had noticed.
🔴 THE HOSTNAME LIST IS DERIVED, NOT TYPED. tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs computes the
deployed set from the tree on every run — Worker custom domains, the app catalogue, and each site's
own canonical URL — and fails when a hostname the repo deploys has no row here. That is the half a
hand-written list can never have: adding a route to a wrangler.jsonc acquires a monitoring
obligation the moment it merges, rather than when somebody remembers this file exists.
⚠️ AND THE CHECK IS DELIBERATELY SPLIT IN TWO.
· tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs   OFFLINE. Runs in ci.yml, reads only the tree, needs no
token and no network. Fails on an undeclared deployed hostname or a dead row.
· tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs          LIVE, AND IT IS A SCHEDULED CI JOB — NOT the hand-run
command this bullet used to call it. OWNER_QUEUE S-8 CLOSED at 2026-08-11T16:55:34Z when
GLITCHTIP_TOKEN became a repository secret (tooling/channel-register.json:813), and
.github/workflows/ops-watch.yml:235 has run it unattended ever since, in the `glitchtip` job, on
FOUR schedules — 07:30, 08:50 and 19:30 UTC daily plus 07:45 UTC Mondays — and on
workflow_dispatch. ⚠️ The script's OWN header still reads 'NOT RUN BY CI, AND THAT IS THE
DESIGN' at tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs:28-34. That header is STALE, and it is not this
file's to fix.
🔴 AND ITS RED IS NOT A CONSOLE MESSAGE — KNOW THE BLAST RADIUS BEFORE EDITING A ROW. It exits
1 on drift, which fails the `glitchtip` job, and ops-watch.yml:258-259 is
`needs: [heartbeats, status, supabase-drift, prod-provenance, runner-budget, glitchtip]` with
`if: failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule'`, whose step opens or comments the
portfolio's SINGLE DURABLE ALERT ISSUE, title 'Scheduled duty is not reporting healthy' —
reused for every later failure and explicitly NEVER closed automatically. So a row here that
describes a monitor the live instance does not have costs a human's attention until that human
closes the issue by hand.
⚠️ THEREFORE A ROW AND ITS LIVE MONITOR ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO. Declaring an `expectedBody`
here before the GlitchTip PUT lands is the SAME DEFECT as a monitor that cannot see a fault,
pointed the other way: a record claiming coverage that does not exist.
· tooling/ops/verify-alarm-chains.mjs      LIVE, and a DIFFERENT question. Everything above asks
'is this host watched'. That asks 'and if the watcher goes red, does a human find out' — the
question nothing was asking while monitor id 6 sat with project_id = NULL, unable to notify
anyone, going Down 13 times of 41 checks. verify-monitors.mjs prints that same monitor as
'not filed under any hostname', correctly and reassuringly, and cannot see the defect. A host
can be fully covered here and still be silent.
That split is why the OFFLINE guard, and only the offline guard, runs on every push: a per-push
limb needing a network token would either be skipped — and a skipped check is a check that reports
ok — or it would make every build depend on the Oracle box, which is the exact single point of
failure the observability note below is about. The live half answers that by running on a SCHEDULE
and gating no merge. But it IS automated and its red IS durable, so read the bullet above before
you edit a row: nothing in this stage is run by hand any more.
⚠️ `monitor: null` IS A GAP, NOT A WAIVER. Those rows are PRINTED on every guard run and never fail
the build. A guard that failed CI on a gap would block every branch on work that is not a change to
this repository. Printing is what stops the gap becoming invisible instead.
🔴 BUT THE REASON THIS PARAGRAPH USED TO GIVE WAS WRONG, AND IT PARKED THE TWO HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE
GAPS IN THE TREE FOR THREE DAYS. It said creating a monitor is 'an action on the owner's GlitchTip
instance rather than a change to this repository', and both gap rows repeated it as 'An owner action'.
It is not: the GlitchTip API takes the vault GLITCHTIP_TOKEN and creates monitors, and on 2026-08-05
an agent did exactly that — twice as throwaways while proving the alert chain, then for real, closing
platform.nikatru.com and config.nikatru.com. Same shape as 'the agent sandbox cannot SSH out', which
survived in four files and parked a whole hardening backlog behind a constraint already disproved.
PROBE A DOCUMENTED LIMIT BEFORE INHERITING IT — and note that BOTH of these were owner-gated in
writing while being fully agent-doable, so the phrase 'owner action' in this file is a claim that
needs evidence, not a category.
⚠️ The gap rows that were closed are kept as `closedGap`, not deleted. A register that erases its
own gaps on closing cannot answer 'how long was this open, and why' — which is the only question
that would have caught the false reason above.
[14]O-2 must CONSUME this register rather than re-enumerate the hostnames. Two enumerations of one
list is how the ceiling budget came to disagree with itself by 5x.

_derivation.workerCustomDomains: every routes[] entry with custom_domain: true across services/*/wrangler.jsonc
_derivation.appCatalogue: every url and api host in catalog/apps.json
_appPublicPathIsCOMPUTEDNotTyped: 🔴 ADDED 2026-09-09 WITH [ADR 075]. An app's published address is no longer a hostname — it is a PATH
on the apex, https://nikatru.com/<id> — so the app's monitor is no longer a `hosts` row of its own. It
is a `pathMonitors` entry on the nikatru.com row, and BOTH of its assertions are RECOMPUTED from the
tree on every run rather than read as text:
· url          = `publicAppUrl(<id>)` + a trailing slash — tooling/sites/apex.mjs, the ONE place the
apex origin is spelled in this repository. catalog/apps.json's `url` is composed
from the same function by tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs, so the register and the
catalogue cannot spell the address differently.
· expectedBody = `<base href="` + `appBaseHref(<id>)` + `">` — same module. That literal is what
`flutter build web --base-href /<id>/` writes into the shell in place of
$FLUTTER_BASE_HREF, so it exists ONLY if a real build ran with the right base href.
· <id>         = the catalogue row's `slug`, which tooling/app-yaml/render.mjs renders from
apps/<id>/app.yaml's `id`. 🔴 THE LITERAL IS NEVER TYPED IN A GUARD. This app has
already been renamed once (the brand moved, the id did not) and app.yaml says the id
may move again; every address in this tree derives from that one field so that a
rename moves BOTH sides of every comparison at once.
tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs performs that computation and exits 1 when a value recorded below
differs from it — so a hand-retyped or stale address in this file is a RED, not a comment nobody reads.
That is what makes the word DERIVED in this register mean the same thing for a path monitor as the
three sources above already make it mean for a hostname.
📌 A GAP THIS BLOCK CAN SEE AND DOES NOT OWN: `appCatalogue` above reads `url` and `api`. The catalogue
row now also carries `origin` (the Pages production alias the apex router fetches from — measured
2026-09-09 as subly-9cp.pages.dev), and tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs does NOT derive it. So
that host is neither derived nor declared and nothing here says whether it should be watched. Named
rather than fixed: assert-monitor-coverage.mjs belongs to another unit.
_derivation.siteCanonicals: the <link rel="canonical"> host of each sites/*/index.html (_shared is not a site)
declared: A hostname NO deploy config can mention, because it is the thing doing the watching.
Exactly one row may carry role: "observability", and the guard requires that row to exist —
otherwise 'is the monitor host itself monitored' is a question nothing in the tree asks.
⚠️ AND IT IS NOT A GENERAL HATCH FOR 'A HOST SOMEBODY MONITORS' — see `_notInThisRegister`
below, which records the 2026-09-03 attempt to widen it and what that attempt measured. 🔴 NOTE
ALSO THAT ONLY REAL SOURCES MAY LIVE IN THIS OBJECT: tooling/ops/status.mjs reads EVERY key here
whose name does not start with an underscore as a derivation source and reports COVERAGE LOST
when one yields no row. Prose belongs at the top level of this file or behind a leading
underscore — a note filed here as a bare key fails [14]O-2's derivation, which is how the first
attempt was caught.
⏱ 2026-09-07 — THIS HATCH NOW CARRIES FIVE ROWS, NOT ONE, AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS APPENDED TO
RATHER THAN REWRITTEN. glitchtip.nikatru.com was joined by the four Box B services — ntfy, vault,
beszel and logs (gap G4 of the 2026-09-07 end-to-end audit: 'nothing watches the pager'). The
widening is DELIBERATE and its bound is unchanged, which is the only reason it is safe:
· A DEPLOYED HOST CANNOT HIDE IN HERE. assert-monitor-coverage.mjs's dead-row limb reaches a
row only after `if (derived.has(h)) continue;` — every hostname the three derived sources
produce is checked by the undeclared limb no matter what its `derivedFrom` says. So the hatch
can admit a host the tree does not deploy; it can never excuse one the tree does.
· role: "observability" is still capped at EXACTLY ONE row by the same guard. The bound was
never the count of `declared` rows — it was that one, and it still holds.
· The 2026-09-03 revert was NOT about the count either. It was reason 2: a row here is an entry
in [14]O-2's unauthenticated probe set, and api-auth.nikatru.com would have gone red while
healthy. ntfy and vault answer an unauthenticated 200 with a probeable body, measured before
the rows were written; beszel and logs cannot be probed from outside without weakening
Cloudflare Access, so they carry `monitor: null` and a stated gap and never enter the probe
set at all. The reason that reverted the first attempt is answered, not overridden.

_notInThisRegister: 🔴 THREE LIVE MONITORS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT ROWS HERE — ids 17, 18 AND 19, ALL CREATED 2026-09-02
and found undeclared on 2026-09-03. Written down because 'absent from this file' and 'nobody has
looked' are indistinguishable, and because the first attempt that day DID add two of them as rows
and had to be reverted. What follows is what that attempt measured.
· 19 `Supabase backup chain` — type Heartbeat. It has no url at all: it asserts that a POST
ARRIVED, not that a host answered, so there is no hostname to file it under. Monitors 6 and 16
have been in exactly this position since they were made, and tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs
prints all three as `not filed under any hostname in the register` on every scheduled run —
correctly, and that print is the whole of what this file can honestly say about them.
· 17 `Supabase auth chain` (auth-api.nikatru.com since [ADR 080], repointed 2026-09-11) and 18 `Studio Access gate`
(studio.nikatru.com) — real hostname monitors, but NOT hostnames this factory deploys: no
wrangler.jsonc route, no catalog/apps.json field, no site canonical, and grep for either string
across the whole tree at HEAD returns zero files. `declared` is not a general escape hatch for
'some host somebody monitors'. It exists for the ONE hostname the derivation structurally
cannot produce — the watcher — and the guard bounds it by requiring that row to exist rather
than by counting, which is only safe while the hatch stays that narrow.
🔴 AND A ROW HERE IS NOT ONLY A DECLARATION — IT IS AN ENTRY IN [14]O-2's PROBE SET. That is the
half the first attempt had not read. tooling/ops/status.mjs derives its surfaces from `hosts`,
probes each one UNAUTHENTICATED from outside, and for any row that declares a `path` it requires
a body that parses as JSON and CARRIES SOMETHING. Measured 2026-09-03 against
auth-api.nikatru.com (api-auth.nikatru.com before [ADR 080]), which has exactly one unauthenticated 200 in the whole of /auth/v1:
· GET /auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json → 200, body {"keys":[]}. An EMPTY array, so status.mjs's
`carries` test is false and the surface reports `vacuous` — RED, on a service that is up.
· GET / → 404, so a row with NO `path` is red on the status limb instead.
· Everything else — /auth/v1/health, /settings, /user, /sso, /logout, /factors, /token,
/admin/users, /oauth/clients, and both other .well-known spellings — answers 401 from the
gateway, without ever reaching GoTrue.
There is no shape of row for that host which O-2 can probe today. A register entry that reddens a
healthy surface teaches people to ignore the prober, and that costs more than the missing row.
⚠️ SO WHERE IS THE COVERAGE? All three ids are in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json →
expectedMonitors, which is keyed by monitor id, asks nothing about hostnames, needs no probe, and
is the ONLY guard in the tree that fails when one of them is deleted. That is the entire
obligation this file would otherwise have carried for them, and it is now carried. 📌 THE DAY
auth-api SERVES AN UNAUTHENTICATED 200 WITH A NON-EMPTY BODY — a populated JWKS would do it — a
row here becomes possible, and this bullet is the thing to delete.
🔴 PHASE 3a/3b, 2026-09-05 — FIVE SERVICES, FOUR NEW PUBLIC HOSTNAMES AND TWO NEW HEARTBEAT
MONITORS, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A ROW HERE. Written down for the same reason as the block above:
'absent from this file' and 'nobody has looked' are indistinguishable, and this is the file a reader
goes to when they want to know whether something is watched.
THE HOSTNAMES, all on the Hostinger box behind one Cloudflare tunnel, no new public port opened:
· vault.nikatru.com   — Vaultwarden 1.37.2, the HUMAN password vault. No Cloudflare Access, on
purpose: an Access 302 breaks every Bitwarden client that is not the web vault.
· ntfy.nikatru.com    — ntfy v2.28.0, the phone alert channel. No Access, ever, at any path: a 302
kills the app's long-lived subscription stream. That one is settled, not deferred.
· beszel.nikatru.com  — Beszel hub 0.19.0, host metrics for BOTH boxes. Behind Access.
· logs.nikatru.com    — Dozzle v10.9.2, read-only container logs. Behind Access.
Also on that box with no hostname at all: Diun 4.33.0 (new-image-tag watcher), restic 0.18.1, and a
native Beszel agent; a second Beszel agent runs on the ORACLE box, which is the one sanctioned
exception to that box being Supabase-only, and it binds the WireGuard address only.
WHY NO ROW, AND IT IS THE SAME TWO REASONS AS 17 AND 18 RATHER THAN A NEW ONE:
1. THIS FILE'S ROWS ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT THIS REPO DEPLOYS. None of the four appears in any
wrangler.jsonc route, in catalog/apps.json, or as a site canonical — measured before this
paragraph was written: `git grep` for all four across the whole tree at the previous commit
returned ZERO files, and this block is now the only place any of them is spelled, which is
prose and not a derivation source. `declared` is the ONE-hostname hatch for the watcher, and
the 2026-09-03 attempt to widen it had to be reverted.
2. A ROW IS ALSO AN ENTRY IN [14]O-2's UNAUTHENTICATED PROBE SET. beszel and logs answer 302 to
the Access login from outside, so tooling/ops/status.mjs would report them red while they are
healthy — a register entry that reddens a working surface teaches people to ignore the prober.
⚠️ SO WHAT ACTUALLY WATCHES THEM TODAY: NOTHING WATCHES THE FOUR HOSTNAMES. That is a real gap and
it is stated rather than implied — no GlitchTip monitor exists for vault, ntfy, beszel or logs, so
any of them can be down indefinitely with every guard in this repo green. What IS watched is the
backup chain that protects their data: GlitchTip heartbeats 22 (`Cloudflare D1/KV backup pull`) and
23 (`Box B restic`), both created 2026-09-05, both declared in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json →
expectedMonitors, and both now carrying a duty row in tooling/ops/register.json
(`duty.cloudflare-backup-pull`, `duty.restic-snapshot`) whose recordQuery reads the monitor by id on
every CI run. Neither is a row here for the reason monitors 6, 16 and 19 are not: a Heartbeat has no
url, so there is no hostname to file it under.
📌 THE SHAPE OF THE CLOSING MOVE, when it is wanted: vault and ntfy answer 200 unauthenticated
(`/alive` and `/`), so those two are the pair a GET monitor could cover today; beszel and logs cannot
be probed from outside without weakening Access, which is not a trade worth making for a dashboard.
And NONE of it narrows `observability.spof` below — every one of these services, the monitors that
would watch them, and both notification hops are on that same single box.
🔴 2026-09-06 — FOUR NEW HEARTBEAT MONITORS, IDS 24 TO 27, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A ROW HERE
EITHER. Recorded for the same reason as every block above: 'absent from this file' and 'nobody has
looked' are indistinguishable, and this is the file a reader opens to find out whether something is
watched.
· 24 `Supabase dump`             — /opt/supabase/backup.sh, every 6h
· 25 `Supabase Drive sync`       — /opt/supabase/sb_drive_sync.sh, every 6h
· 26 `Supabase second-copy sync` — /opt/supabase/sb_boxb_sync.sh, every 6h
· 27 `Supabase disk alert`       — /opt/supabase/disk-alert.py, hourly
All four are type Heartbeat in project `ops`, all four beat through /opt/supabase/hb-run.sh on the
AUTH box, and all four are now read by name in tooling/ops/register.json — `duty.supabase-dump`,
`duty.supabase-drive-sync`, `duty.supabase-second-copy` and `duty.supabase-disk-alert` — whose
`recordQuery` resolves each monitor by id on every CI run. The fifth cron on that box,
/opt/supabase/backup-liveness.py, keeps posting to monitor 19, which has existed since 2026-09-02
and is named three blocks above; `duty.supabase-backup-liveness` is what finally reads it.
WHY NO ROW, AND IT IS THE FIRST OF THE TWO REASONS ONLY: a Heartbeat has NO URL. It asserts that a
POST arrived, not that a host answered, so there is no hostname to file it under — exactly the
position monitors 6, 16, 19, 22 and 23 have been in since they were made. The second reason (a row
here is an entry in [14]O-2's unauthenticated probe set) does not even arise, because there is
nothing to probe. tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs prints all nine as `not filed under any hostname
in the register` on every scheduled run, correctly, and that print is the whole of what this file
can honestly say about them.
🔴 ONE THING HERE IS BETTER THAN ANYTHING ELSE THIS FILE RECORDS, AND IT SHOULD NOT BE ROUNDED IN
WITH THE REST: these five duties are watched from a DIFFERENT BOX than the one they run on. Every
other cron row in tooling/ops/register.json is watched by a monitor on its own machine, which is
the failure `observability.spof` below is about. The auth box dying leaves the monitors, the alert
evaluation and both notification hops alive. It does not narrow `observability.spof` — that gap is
about the SERVICES box, where all of this watching lives, and it is exactly as open as it was.
⏱ 2026-09-07 — THE 2026-09-05 BLOCK ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED IN ONE SENTENCE AND LEFT STANDING IN THE
REST. That block's ⚠️ line reads 'NOTHING WATCHES THE FOUR HOSTNAMES'. As of today two of the four
are watched and the other two are ROWS in `hosts` above rather than paragraphs here, so this file
no longer needs a block to say they exist. The 2026-09-05 wording is kept verbatim because it was
true on its date and because the reasoning in it — why a Heartbeat has no hostname, why an
Access-fronted host cannot be probed from outside — is unchanged and still load-bearing.
WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED (gap G4 of the 2026-09-07 end-to-end audit, 'nothing watches the pager'):
· monitor 31 `ntfy.nikatru.com`  — GET https://ntfy.nikatru.com/v1/health, 200, body
"healthy":true, every 60 s, confirmationThreshold 2, project `ops`. Created 06:34:49Z.
· monitor 32 `vault.nikatru.com` — GET https://vault.nikatru.com/alive, 200, body Z", every
60 s, confirmationThreshold 2, project `ops`. Created 06:34:49Z, and PROVEN BY BREAKING IT the
same hour: down at 06:37:06Z, on the phone topic at 06:37:09Z, restored and back up at
06:38:17Z. The full record is in that row's `closedGap.🔴 forcedDownProof`.
· beszel.nikatru.com and logs.nikatru.com are rows with `monitor: null` and a stated gap, so
assert-monitor-coverage.mjs names them on stdout on every single run.
⏱ 2026-09-15 — NO LONGER: both rows now carry Heartbeat monitor 39 `Box B dashboards origin`,
fed by an origin-side poster on Box B over loopback (closure (a) of their own gap action). It
asserts ORIGIN health only; the tunnel is the platform Worker's boxbReachability probe. Each
row keeps its gap as `closedGap`. Ids 38 and 39 are in expectedMonitors too.
Both new ids are in tooling/ops/alarm-chains.json → expectedMonitors, which is still the only
guard in the tree that fails when a monitor is deleted and recreated.
🔴 AND IT NARROWS `observability.spof` BY NOTHING AT ALL, for the third time in this file. The two
new monitors run inside GlitchTip on Box B; ntfy runs on Box B; the webhook hop is on Box B. If
that box is gone, the pager and the thing watching the pager are gone together and neither says
so. What the ntfy monitor buys is the failure that actually happens to containers — one service
down while the box is up — and in that case the alert leaves by alert rule 2's EMAIL recipient,
through Resend, off this box. E-9b is exactly as open as it was on 2026-08-03.
📌 STILL UNDECLARED, MEASURED THE SAME DAY: live monitors 29 `Laptop routine: ops check` and 30
`Laptop routine: CI watchdog` (Heartbeats, created 2026-09-06) are in NEITHER this file (correctly
— a Heartbeat has no hostname) NOR alarm-chains.json → expectedMonitors (which is the gap: nothing
would notice either being deleted). Named here rather than fixed because they are the routines
unit's rows, not this one's.

hosts.what: the factory's public site — and since [ADR 075] the address EVERY app is published at, as a path: https://nikatru.com/<id>
🔴 whyThisRowCarriesASECONDList: `monitor` above watches the apex DOOR — `/`, and the marketing site's canonical tag. `pathMonitors`
below watches what the apex now SERVES UNDER that door: since [ADR 075] each app is published at
https://nikatru.com/<id>, so an app's monitor is no longer a hostname row of its own.
⚠️ AND IT IS A SECOND LIST RATHER THAN A SECOND ROW BECAUSE A SECOND ROW IS FORBIDDEN, DELIBERATELY.
tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs fails on a duplicate hostname — "Two rows for one hostname is
two answers to 'is it monitored'" — and tooling/ops/status.mjs refuses the same shape for the same
reason. Both are right and neither was weakened to make room for this: `hostname` still answers
exactly one question and still has exactly one answer. What changed is that a hostname is no longer
the unit an app is published at, so a per-hostname register needed somewhere to put a per-PATH check,
and the safe place is inside the row for the host that serves the path.
🔴 WHO READS IT. tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs, in the same change that added it — it reconciles
every entry against the live GlitchTip instance on the same four limbs it applies to `monitor` (the
id exists, the live host matches, the type matches, a declared body matches verbatim) and it
RECOMPUTES `url` and `expectedBody` from the tree first, per `_derivation._appPublicPathIsCOMPUTEDNot
Typed`. Both directions are checked: a catalogue app published on the apex with no entry here is a
failure, and an entry here that no catalogue app produces is a failure. A register earns JSON only
when a guard reads it.
📌 WHAT DOES *NOT* READ IT, MEASURED 2026-09-09 AND STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED:
tooling/ci/assert-monitor-coverage.mjs grades `monitor` only, so its limb 4 ("a claimed monitor is a
complete claim") does not reach these entries, and tooling/ops/status.mjs probes `monitor` only, so
[14]O-2 does not probe https://nikatru.com/<id>/ from outside. Neither file belongs to the unit that
wrote this block. Until they do, the OFFLINE per-push half of E-9 is blind to this list and the
SCHEDULED half is not — which is the opposite of the split the top of this file describes, and it is
written down here so the next reader inherits the gap rather than the impression of coverage.

pathMonitors.name: Subscription Tracker web
🔴 verifiedOnIsNullAndThatIsTheHONESTValu: It read 2026-08-11 while this monitor watched https://subly.nikatru.com/ and asserted
`<base href="/">`. BOTH of those assertions are being replaced by this change and NEITHER new
value has been read off the live instance, because the live instance still carries the old ones.
A date here would be this file claiming a verification nobody performed — the exact defect the
`monitor: null` paragraph at the top of this file exists to refuse, pointed at a field instead of
a row. It becomes a date on the day the PUT below lands and verify-monitors.mjs exits 0.
🔴 SO THIS ENTRY IS RED UNTIL THE DEPLOY, ON PURPOSE, AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS REAL. Until the
migration ships AND the PUT below is made, tooling/ops/verify-monitors.mjs exits 1 on this entry.
In the SCHEDULED `glitchtip` job (.github/workflows/ops-watch.yml) that exit opens this
portfolio's single durable alert issue, which is never closed automatically. That is why this
file's own rule is 'A ROW AND ITS LIVE MONITOR ARE ONE CHANGE, NOT TWO' — and on this branch the
two ARE one change: the branch that publishes the app on the apex is the branch that must make
the PUT. Merging the first without the second is the state this red is warning about, not a
false alarm to be waited out.
⚠️ THE ALTERNATIVE WAS CONSIDERED AND REFUSED. subscriptiontracker-api.nikatru.com carried a
`🔴 openBodyGap` block until 2026-09-12, when its matcher landed live (git history holds the
block). It showed the other move: WITHDRAW the assertion into a gap block so the declared-body
limb has nothing to compare and the scheduled job stays green. That is right when the register would
otherwise claim MORE coverage than exists. Here it would claim LESS than the truth in the
direction that hides a fault: the old body `<base href="/">` is what a build published at the
OLD address serves, so a withdrawn assertion plus a shipped migration is a monitor that stays
green while pointed at a retired subdomain — a check that silently stopped checking, which this
repository's verification discipline puts above a noisy one.

theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.🔴 fullReplace: PUT IS A FULL REPLACE — re-send name, monitorType, expectedStatus, interval, timeout, confirmationThreshold AND `project` unchanged alongside the two fields above, then DIFF the read-back. Omitting `project` silently detaches the monitor from every alert recipient under an HTTP 200; that is monitor 6's defect and it happened to all nine monitors at once on 2026-08-11 (tooling/channel-register.json, [ADR 043]).
theLiveChangeThatClosesThis.orderMatters: The PUT must land AFTER the apex router serves the app, not before: pointed at https://nikatru.com/<id>/ one minute early it is red for a reason that is not a fault. across four saves and three url spellings (https://nikatru.com, the same with a trailing
slash, https://glitchtip.nikatru.com), with timeout 20 and with null, with expectedStatus
null and with 200, and — the part that rules out a scheduling artefact — on THREE
consecutive SCHEDULED checks at 10:08:26Z, 10:09:27Z and 10:10:27Z that no save triggered.
· THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THIS A FINDING RATHER THAN A GUESS. The same monitor id, the same
url, switched to monitorType GET, answered UP in 70 ms 0.6 s later. Only the type changed.
· AND THE CERTIFICATE IS FINE: `openssl x509 -enddate` against nikatru.com the same day reads
notAfter Oct 14 2026 — 41 days out.
· 📌 READ THE FIRST CHECK ROW CAREFULLY IF YOU REPEAT THIS. Every save writes an instant
`isUp:false, responseTime:0` row before the real check lands, so ONE down row proves nothing
at all — the GET control produced exactly that row too, 0.6 s before it went up. The finding
is that for SSL no real row ever followed it.
So an SSL monitor created here today would be RED from the moment it existed, on a host whose
certificate is valid, and it would mail a human about it every day. Nine of those is not
coverage; it is this register learning to lie in the other direction.
⚠️ SO NOTHING WAS DECLARED IN ITS PLACE, and that is the point of writing this down instead. No
row above carries an `sslMonitor` field, because a row claiming a check nobody is running is the
same defect as a check that cannot see a fault, pointed the other way — the rule
subscriptiontracker-api.nikatru.com's `🔴 openBodyGap` block applied to a body matcher until that
matcher landed live on 2026-09-12 and the block was deleted with it.
